title: 1  Shrimp Year Abundance Index Explanation
text:
1.1 Shrimp Year
When examining long-term datasets, it is convenient, if not necessary, to perform some aggregation of data to means or totals over some representative length of time (e.g. monthly mean temperature, annual precipitation total, monthly or annual totals of money spent on [anything related to budgets]).
In this project, we want to be able to link different life stages of shrimp to each other, and ask questions like “if postlarvae did well this year, did juveniles also do well? does that hold all the way through adults, and fisheries landings?”
Animal life cycles, incoveniently for us, do not necessarily align with calendar years. It may be (and for brown shrimp generally is the case) that young are spawned early in a calendar year and are adults late in that calendar year. However, white shrimp (and many other species) may be spawned in the middle or late part of a calendar year, and not be adults until the next calendar year. So, in order to relate those adults to the earlier life stages, we cannot use calendar year to represent the cohort of shrimp.
We use shrimp year to represent a single cohort of shrimp, and assign the calendar year in which that group of shrimp will live most of their lives. For brown shrimp, the shrimp year is the calendar year in which the individuals will show up in the fishery. For white shrimp, it is the year in which they go through most life stages; though adults will bleed into (and spawn in) the following calendar year.
Each survey in this project, based on its location of sampling, is expected to primarily catch a single life stage of each shrimp. Based on the month of sampling, the targeted life stage, and the shrimp species, we assigned shrimp year to each sampling event based on the following:

Environmental data
Winter temperatures and cold spells can impact shrimp growth and/or survival, and understanding these dynamics is important to shrimp fishery managers. Salinity during early life stages may also impact shrimp, and these effects extend to later stages of the life cycle.
Again, we need to aggregate data. Winter here is defined as December through February. For brown shrimp, the shrimp year impacted by winter temperatures is the calendar year containing that January and February. For white shrimp, we have assigned each winter metric separately to two life stages, as they occur in different years: postlarval winters and adult winters. Subadults and adults will be impacted by winter temperatures occurring a year after the winter temperatures that affect the postlarval and juvenile stages. See Figure 1.1. Nursery period is defined separately for each species, based on Batchelder et al. 2024*: April through July for brown shrimp, and June through October for white shrimp.
*Batchelder, L., Stone, J., Kimball, M., Pfirrmann, B., & Dunn, R. (2024). Phenology of penaeid shrimp nursery habitat use: Trends and environmental drivers over four decades. Marine Ecology Progress Series, 751, 79–95. https://doi.org/10.3354/meps14741

text:
1.3 Abundance Index
This project brought together a number of surveys by different organizations, with different methods, and different ways of quantifying shrimp abundance. In order to make these numbers comparable, while accounting for possible variation in the number of sampling stations and sample dates over time, we have adjusted abundance metrics to an index using the following steps. More details for individual datasets will be provided in that life stage’s chapter in the “Summarizing to Abundance Index” portion of this book.
For each survey:

Assign shrimp year to each sample, based on month and species.

If a sampling event (site/station on a date) had replicates, average them.

Average data across all sites/stations on a sample day.

Average data across all sampling dates within each month = average abundance for the month.

Add the monthly averages, to get a total abundance for each shrimp year. This absorbs variability in timing for a year.

From total abundance per shrimp year, derive an index:

Take the square root of total abundance (deals some with extreme high numbers).

Mean-center the result from (a) across all shrimp years for the dataset.

Divide by the standard deviation across all shrimp years for the datset.

ch <- readxl::read_xlsx(here::here(in_path, "SCDNR_CHS_TempData_ 1950_2024.xlsx"))

# pivot

Consecutive days below thresholds
There is some debate over which temperature threshold is most important. Here, we compare to each temperature from 7-16C.


Code
ch_winter <- ch2 |> 
    # filter to winter, assign shrimp year, grab only complete shrimp years
    filter(Month %in% c(12, 1, 2)) |> 
    mutate(shrimp_year = case_when(Month == 12 ~ Year + 1,
                                   .default = Year)) |> 
    filter(shrimp_year >= 1951,
           shrimp_year <= 2023) |> 
    group_by(shrimp_year) 

thresholds <- 7:16
consec_out <- list()
for(i in seq_along(thresholds)){
    consec_out[[i]] <- ch_winter |> 
        group_by(shrimp_year) |> 
        summarize(stats = consec_stats(waterTempC, thresholds[i])) |> 
        unnest_wider(stats)
}

tmp_thresh <- bind_rows(consec_out)

tmp_thresh <- tmp_thresh |> 
    rename(calendar_year = shrimp_year)




Code
ggplot(tmp_thresh,
       aes(x = calendar_year,
           col = threshold)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = totalDays,
                  linetype = "total # days")) +
    geom_line(aes(y = longestSpell,
                  linetype = "longest consecutive # days")) +
    facet_wrap(~threshold, ncol = 3) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "Winter temperatures at CHS",
         subtitle = "By temperature threshold (panels)",
         x = "Year",
         y = "# days") +
    scale_color_continuous(guide = "none") +
    theme(legend.position = "top")

title: 3  Environmental Data
text:
3.2 Salinity
Nursery period salinity was important to phenology in Batchelder et al. 2024. We define nursery periods as per that manuscript: Apr-Jul for brown shrimp and Jun-Oct for white shrimp. I use both ‘calendar_year’ and ‘shrimp_year’ here because even though they are the same by our definitions (see Table 1.1), it can be a little difficult to keep track of - so I’m being as explicit as possible.
Here we pull data from the stations CH07, CH09, CH10, and CH18.


Code
trawl_dat <- read.csv(here::here(in_path,
                                 "SCDNR_EstuarineTrawlShrimpSize.csv"))


Salinity at each station was averaged to the day and month. There was at least one anomalously high value, so a line of code removed any values above 50.


Code
# there's a row for every shrimp; condense to one row per trawl  
dat <- trawl_dat |> 
    select(Coll, Year, Month, Day, StationCode, SalinityB) |> 
    filter(StationCode %in% c("CH07", "CH09", "CH10", "CH18")) |> 
    distinct() |> 
    arrange(Year, Month, StationCode)

# for each station, average to the day and to the month
# there was an anomalously high value in here so first
# replace anything over 50 with NA
dat_monthly <- dat |> 
    mutate(SalinityB = case_when(SalinityB > 50 ~ NA_real_,
                                 .default = SalinityB)) |> 
    summarize(.by = c(StationCode, Year, Month, Day),
              sal = mean(SalinityB, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
    summarize(.by = c(StationCode, Year, Month),
              sal = mean(sal, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
    pivot_wider(names_from = StationCode,
                names_prefix = "sal_",
                values_from = sal) |> 
    rowwise() |> 
    mutate(sal_mean07.09.10 = mean(c(sal_CH07, sal_CH09, sal_CH10), na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
    ungroup() |>   # leaving out CH18 because it doesn't start until the mid-80s and really affects the mean
    pivot_longer(all_of(starts_with("sal")),
                 names_to = "station",
                 names_prefix = "sal_",
                 values_to = "sal")

# each species has different nursery periods - subset and assign appropriate shrimp years
brown_nursery <- dat_monthly |> 
    filter(Month %in% c(4:7))

brown_nursery_byYear <- brown_nursery |> 
    summarize(.by = c(station, Year),
              sal = mean(sal, na.rm = TRUE))

brown_byYear_wide <- brown_nursery_byYear |> 
    pivot_wider(names_from = station,
                values_from = sal) |> 
    rename(calendar_year = Year) |> 
    mutate(species = "brown",
           shrimp_year = calendar_year) |> 
    relocate(species, calendar_year, shrimp_year)

Input data file(s) - as-used; can be found in data/raw/environmental:

Modifications to data:
Summary calculations, described below for each output data frame.
Generated data file(s):
Data frames were modified as described above, and written to data/intermediate/environmental_dfs.RData (the single .RData file contains multiple data frames):

tmp_thresh - counts of days below temperature thresholds for each year.
calendar year represents the year containing January and February. Because we defined winter as December-February, calendar_year 2004 summarizes the time period December 2003 - February 2004.

threshold column contains each integer from 7-16, representing degrees C.
totalDays is the total number of days in that time period below the threshold in the threshold column.

totalSpells represents how many times there were at least 7 consecutive days below the given threshold.

longestSpell is the longest stretch of consecutive days (with a minimum of at least 7) within the time period.

tmp_distn follows the same calendar_year scheme as tmp_thresh. In this data frame, there is only one column for each ‘calendar_year’. Columns represent which ‘shrimp year’ the calendar year would fall into for each species/life stage, followed by summary statistics for water temperature over Dec-Feb: min, median, max, mean, sd, iqr, etc.

sal_means contains one row for each ‘shrimp year’ (matches calendar year) and species. Columns are average nursery period salinity from each of 4 stations, and one column containing the mean from 3 of the four stations (one station was less like the others). Nursery periods were defined as in Batchelder et al. 2024; see above for more.

The data files to be used further in the workflow combined temperature and salinity information for each year x species, and were separated by species. These are both saved in data/processed/environmental. Each has a single row per shrimp year. For white shrimp, there are columns for each of ‘postlarval winter’ and ‘subadult winter’, along with columns identifying which calendar year was used for the calculations, because the white shrimp life cycle is much trickier than brown:

In these plots, there is a panel for each shrimp species. Size is represented on the y-axis, and a cloud of points called a “beeswarm” has representation for every data point. Each point is colored by the numeric month in which the individual was caught, allowing us to see differences in size at different parts of the year and life-cycle.
There are three different measures of size in this dataset: Rostrum length, Telson length, and Uropod length. A graph is below for each.

The y-axis represents length. More points spread out along the x-axis for a given length means that there were more individuals of that length captured than regions where points remain closer to the center.

The y-axis represents length. title: 5  Juveniles
text:
5.1 Datasets
There are two datasets that represent juveniles: SCDNR’s Creek Trawls, and NIW NERR’s Oyster Landing seines. We will explore each.
Code
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(readxl)
library(ggbeeswarm)

source("functions.R")

in_path <- here::here("data", "raw", "juv")

surv_sc <- "SCDNR Creek Trawls"
surv_ol <- "Oyster Landing Seines"
Code
juv_sc_cpue <- read.csv(here::here(in_path, "SCDNR_CreekTrawlShrimpCPUE.csv"))
juv_sc_size <- read.csv(here::here(in_path, "SCDNR_CreekTrawlShrimpSize.csv"))

juv_ol <- read.csv(here::here(in_path, 
                              "Oyster Landing Seine Shrimp Dataset - 1984-2023 (BWP, 2025-04-24)(kac 2025-06-02).csv"))
Code
# Pull out date characteristics and deal with column types if necessary; change Species columns to common names.  

juv_sc_size <- juv_sc_size |> 
    mutate(Date = lubridate::mdy(DTStart),
           Year = lubridate::year(Date),
           Month = lubridate::month(Date),
           Species = case_when(Species == "Penaeus aztecus" ~ "brown",
                               Species == "Penaeus setiferus" ~ "white",
                               Species == "Penaeus duorarum" ~ "pink",
                               .default = "uh-oh"))

juv_sc_cpue <- juv_sc_cpue |> 
    mutate(Species = case_when(Species == "Penaeus aztecus" ~ "brown",
                               Species == "Penaeus setiferus" ~ "white",
                               Species == "Penaeus duorarum" ~ "pink",
                               .default = "uh-oh"))

juv_ol <- juv_ol |> 
    mutate(Date = lubridate::mdy(Date),
           Month = lubridate::month(Date),
           Temp = case_when(Temp == "DataGap" ~ NA_character_,
                            Temp == "" ~ NA_character_,
                            .default = Temp),
           Sal = case_when(Sal == "DataGap" ~ NA_character_,
                           Sal == "" ~ NA_character_,
                           .default = Sal),
           Weight = case_when(Weight == "." ~ NA_character_,
                              .default = Weight),
           Temp = as.numeric(Temp),
           Sal = as.numeric(Sal),
           Weight = as.numeric(Weight),
           Species = case_when(Species == "Farfantepenaeus aztecus" ~ "brown",
                               Species == "Litopenaeus setiferus" ~ "white",
                               .default = "uh-oh"))

           starts_with("LEN")) |>

                 names_to = "Rep",

    filter(!is.na(Length))

title: 6  Subadults
text:
6.1 Datasets
There are two datasets that represent subadults: GADNR’s EMTS sampling and SCDNR’s Estuarine Trawls. We will explore each.
Code
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(readxl)
library(ggbeeswarm)

source("functions.R")

in_path <- here::here("data", "raw", "subad")

surv_ga <- "GADNR EMTS"
surv_sc <- "SCDNR Estuarine Trawls"
Code
# GA Counts
subad_ga_count_brown <- read_xlsx(here::here(in_path, "GADNR_EMTS_PenaeidShrimp_Brown_Count_thru2021.xlsx"),
                                  na = c("", ".")) |> 
    mutate(Species = "brown")
# looks from early exploration like NumperLb was mis-calculated when the sample weight wasn't the typical 1360.78 - it used that value anyway (this happened when catch was low)
subad_ga_count_white <- read_xlsx(here::here(in_path, "GADNR_EMTS_PenaeidShrimp_White_Count_thru2021.xlsx"),
                                  na = c("", "."))  |> 
    mutate(Species = "white")

# GA Sizes
subad_ga_size_brown <- read_xlsx(here::here(in_path, "GADNR_EMTS_PenaeidShrimp_SIZE_thru2021.xlsx"),
                                 sheet = "Brown shrimp") |> 
    mutate(Species = "brown")
subad_ga_size_white <- read_xlsx(here::here(in_path, "GADNR_EMTS_PenaeidShrimp_SIZE_thru2021.xlsx"),
                                 sheet = "White Shrimp")  |> 
    mutate(Species = "white")

# SC
subad_sc_cpue <- read.csv(here::here(in_path, "SCDNR_EstuarineTrawlShrimpCPUE.csv"))
subad_sc_size <- read.csv(here::here(in_path, "SCDNR_EstuarineTrawlShrimpSize.csv")) |> 
    filter(Length < 1000)  # there was a goof in the file somewhere
Code
# Combine species in GA data frames; pull out date characteristics and deal with column types if necessary; change shrimp species to common names. 

subad_ga_count <- bind_rows(subad_ga_count_brown, subad_ga_count_white) |> 
    mutate(GuessedDate = lubridate::ymd(substr(RefNum, 3, 8)),
           Year = lubridate::year(GuessedDate),
           Month = lubridate::month(GuessedDate))
subad_ga_size <- bind_rows(subad_ga_size_brown, subad_ga_size_white) |> 
    mutate(Date = lubridate::mdy(TowDate),
           Year = lubridate::year(Date),
           Month = lubridate::month(Date))

subad_sc_cpue <- subad_sc_cpue |> 
    mutate(Species = case_when(Species == "Penaeus aztecus" ~ "brown",
                               Species == "Penaeus setiferus" ~ "white",
                               Species == "Penaeus duorarum" ~ "pink",
                               .default = "uh-oh"))

subad_sc_size <- subad_sc_size |> 
    mutate(Species = case_when(Species == "Penaeus aztecus" ~ "brown",
                               Species == "Penaeus setiferus" ~ "white",
                               Species == "Penaeus duorarum" ~ "pink",
                               .default = "uh-oh"))
Code
# save to use later
save(subad_ga_count, subad_ga_size,
     subad_sc_cpue, subad_sc_size,
     file = here::here("data",
                       "intermediate",
                       "subadult_dfs.RData"),
     compress = "xz")

6.2 Graphics - Size Distributions
South Carolina’s file has over 300,000 points, which makes for a beeswarm plot that is very large and slow to render. Georgia’s file is “only” 65k and even it is too slow to render beeswarm plots. So rather than graphing the full datasets, I have randomly sampled 10,000 rows from GA and 15,000 rows from SC (because SC has three species).


Code
set.seed(1234)
# subsample GA
subad_ga_sizeb_ind <- sample(1:nrow(subad_ga_size), size = 10000, replace = FALSE)
subad_ga_sizeb <- subad_ga_size[subad_ga_sizeb_ind, ]
# subsample SC
subad_sc_sizeb_ind <- sample(1:nrow(subad_sc_size), size = 15000, replace = FALSE)
subad_sc_sizeb <- subad_sc_size[subad_sc_sizeb_ind, ]




Code
# make plots
beeswarm_sizeDistn(subad_ga_sizeb,
                   x = "Species", y = "Size", month = "Month",
                   survey = surv_ga)








Figure 6.1: Beeswarm plot of subadult shrimp length for the GADNR data. Points represent measurements of individual shrimp, and are colored by the month in which they were captured. The y-axis represents length. More points spread out along the x-axis for a given length means that there were more individuals of that length captured than regions where points remain closer to the center.







Code
beeswarm_sizeDistn(subad_sc_sizeb,
                   x = "Species", y = "Length", month = "Month",
                   survey = surv_sc)








Figure 6.2: Beeswarm plot of subadult shrimp length for the SCDNR data. Points represent measurements of individual shrimp, and are colored by the month in which they were captured. The y-axis represents length. More points spread out along the x-axis for a given length means that there were more individuals of that length captured than regions where points remain closer to the center.

title: 6  Subadults
text:
6.3 Graphics - Abundance/CPUE Boxplots


Code
p1 <- subad_sc_cpue |> 
    mutate(TotNum = CPUE + 0.0001) |> 
    ggplot() + 
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(Month),
                     y = CPUE,
                     fill = Month)) +
    facet_wrap(~Species, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_y_log10() +
    khroma::scale_fill_YlOrBr() +
    labs(title = "CPUE in SCDNR Estuarine Trawls",
         x = "Month") +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

p2 <- subad_ga_count |> 
    mutate(Count = TotNum + 0.001) |> 
    ggplot() +
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(Month),
                   y = Count,
                   fill = Month)) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    khroma::scale_fill_YlOrBr() +
    facet_wrap(~Species, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(title = "Count in GA EMTS",
         x = "Month") +
    theme(legend.position = "none")


p1 + p2








Figure 6.3: Boxplots representing shrimp abundance (as either CPUE or count, depending on the survey) by month. Note the log10-scaled y-axes.





Both surveys (unsurprisingly) show the same temporal pattern of abundance - brown shrimp most abundant in June and July, also high in August; and May in SC. For white shrimp, we see a dip in June and (less so) July.

7.1 Datasets
There are two SEAMAP files: one of events, and one of catch data.
Code
library(tidyverse)

source("functions.R")

surv <- "SEAMAP"
Code
seamap <- read.csv(here::here(in_path, "SEAMAP_ShrimpCatches_19892022.csv"))
Code
# rename, make dates, deal with columns
sm <- seamap |> 
    select(Date = DATE,
           Event = EVENTNAME,
           Collection = COLLECTIONNUMBER,
           Species = SPECIESCOMMONNAME,
           Count = NUMBERTOTAL,
           Weight = SPECIESTOTALWEIGHT,
           DepthZone = DEPTHZONE,
           Region = REGION) |> 
    mutate(Date = lubridate::mdy(Date),
           Year = lubridate::year(Date),
           Month = lubridate::month(Date),
           Species = case_when(str_detect(Species, "BROWN") ~ "brown",
                               str_detect(Species, "WHITE") ~ "white",
                               str_detect(Species, "PINK") ~ "pink",
                               .default = "noneMaybe"))
Looks like when no shrimp were caught in a net, the species is left blank and count and weight are both 0. So I’ll widen the data frame, filling in 0s for NAs. Then lengthen back out so 0s are all accounted for.
Also filtering to “INNER” depth zone.
Code
adsm_wide <- sm |> 
    filter(DepthZone == "INNER") |> 
    select(Date, Year, Month, Region, Event, Collection, Species, Weight, Count) |> 
    pivot_wider(names_from = Species,
                values_from = c(Weight, Count),
                values_fill = 0) |> 
    select(-ends_with("noneMaybe"))

adsm_long <- pivot_longer(adsm_wide,
                        cols = c(all_of(starts_with("Weight")),
                                 all_of(starts_with("Count"))),
                        names_to = c(".value", "species"),
                        names_sep = "_")
Weight and count were both recorded, even in subsamples, BUT “when large numbers of a species occurred in the processed catch”, all individuals were weighed; a subsample was processed for abundance (typically 32-64 individuals); and count was estimated from the weight.
FOR THAT REASON I will use weights in my analyses, because it is the most likely piece to have been measured rather than estimated.
Code

save(seamap, adsm_long, adsm_wide,
     file = here::here("data",
                       "intermediate",

     compress = "xz")

title: 8  Adults - landings and trip tickets
text:
8.1 Datasets
There are three files that represent commercial fisheries data for adult shrimp: Landings, from NMFS, at two different frequencies (annual for both species, and for white shrimp, fall vs. winter-spring-summer); and trip tickets, by 2-month blocks for both species.
For brown shrimp, calendar year is fine. White shrimp have different life cycles, and we are interested in spawning adults vs. non-spawning adults for each ‘shrimp year’; so we obtained the head-off white shrimp data file, split into seasons.
Code
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(readxl)
library(ggbeeswarm)

source("functions.R")

in_path <- here::here("data", "raw", "ad_commercial")

surv_tripTicks <- "Trip Tickets"
surv_NMFS_annual <- "NMFS Annual Landings"  # use for brown shrimp
surv_NMFS_seasonal <- "NMFS Seasonal Landings"  # use for white shrimp
Code
# Trip Ticket Abundances
tripTick_abund <- readxl::read_xlsx(here::here(in_path,
                                               "Nonconfidential Shrimp landings by species area year two month block.xlsx"),
                                    sheet = "Nonconfidential Shrimp landings") 

# Trip Ticket locations
# based on assignments from Kim during exploratory mapping
tripTick_locs <- read.csv(here::here(in_path,
                                     "Nonconfidential Shrimp landings areas.csv")) |> 
    select(Area.name, State)


# Annual Landings (focus on Brown)
landings_annual <- read.csv(here::here(in_path,
                            "Shrimp Landings NC SC GA from NMFS.csv")) 


# Seasonal Landings (White)
landings_seas <- read.csv(here::here(in_path,
                                     "scga_landings_headOff_whiteShrimp_byseason.csv"))
Code
# deal with column types, naming, etc.
tripTick_abund <- tripTick_abund |> 
    mutate(Species = case_match(Common.Name,
                                "NORTHERN PINK" ~ "pink",
                                "NORTHERN BROWN" ~ "brown",
                                "NORTHERN WHITE" ~ "white",
                                "PENAEID" ~ "Penaeid"),
           CPUE_approx = annland / numdeal,
           Wave = case_match(WAVE,
                             1 ~ "1 Jan-Feb",
                             2 ~ "2 Mar-Apr",
                             3 ~ "3 May-Jun",
                             4 ~ "4 Jul-Aug",
                             5 ~ "5 Sep-Oct",
                             6 ~ "6 Nov-Dec"),
           Wave_start = case_match(WAVE,      # so it can show up approximately correctly in time series graphs
                                        1 ~ 1,
                                        2 ~ 3,
                                        3 ~ 5,
                                        4 ~ 7,
                                        5 ~ 9,
                                        6 ~ 11))  |> 
    # join states
    left_join(tripTick_locs, by = "Area.name")


landings_annual <- landings_annual |> 
    mutate(Species = case_match(NMFS.Name,
                                "SHRIMP, NORTHERN BROWN " ~ "brown",
                                "SHRIMP, NORTHERN PINK " ~ "pink",
                                "SHRIMP, NORTHERN WHITE " ~ "white",
                                "SHRIMPS, PENAEID **" ~ "Penaeid"),
           Pounds = parse_number(Pounds),
           Dollars = parse_number(Dollars),
           Millions_of_dollars = Dollars / 1000000,
           Millions_of_Pounds = Pounds / 1000000)

landings_seas <- landings_seas  |> 
    mutate(Species = "white",
           Months = case_match(season,
                               "Fall" ~ "2 Aug-Dec",
                               "Win_Spr_Sum" ~ "1 Jan-Jul"),
           Period = case_match(season,                   # because Win/Spr/Sum is earlier in the year than Fall, but it shows up later when sorted alphabetically
                               "Fall" ~ 2,
                               "Win_Spr_Sum" ~ 1)) |> 
    arrange(Year, Period) |> 
    select(-X)

title: 8  Adults - landings and trip tickets
text:
8.4 About
Input .qmd file for this section was: raw_ad_commercial.qmd and can be found in the main directory.
Input data file(s) - as-used; can be found in data/raw/ad_commercial:

Nonconfidential Shrimp landings by species area year two month block.xlsx - Trip Tickets. Commercial shrimp landings in NC, SC, GA, and FL, by 2-month block, as reported by commercial fishers and seafood processors. From state trip ticket data. per the data provider, this dataset probably best if we’re interested in estimating CPUE. ” Trip tickets, which have area fished, came online at different times (GA 1999, SC 2003, NC 1994). That is causing the differences. Also NC didn’t always differentiate among the species (I think 96 to 98). ”
Shrimp Landings NC SC GA from NMFS.csv - both species, calendar year level (okay for brown shrimp, not white). Annual commercial shrimp landings in NC, SC, and GA, as reported by commercial fishers and seafood processors, and downloaded from https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/foss/f?p=215:200:::::: per the data provider, this dataset is probably the better one for total landings.
scga_landings_headOff_whiteShrimp_byseason.csv - white shrimp, by Fall vs. Winter-Spring-Summer. Combined white shrimp landings for SC and GA by two ‘seasons’. The Fall is defined as Aug-Dec and the Win_Spr_Sum is defined as Jan-July. As such, these two seasons can be combined to come up with ‘Annual’ landings.

Modifications to data:

All files: changed Species from provided names to ‘brown’, ‘white’, and ‘pink’.

Trip Tickets file: Calculated CPUE_approx as landings / number of dealers (number of dealers and number of fishers were the same). Made two new columns for two-month WAVE: Wave to identify the months, e.g. 1 Jan-Feb, 2 Mar-Apr, etc.; and Wave_start to identify the first month numerically, for better plotting of time series, e.g. Wave 1 (Jan-Feb) is assigned 1; Wave 2 (Mar-Apr) is assigned 3; etc. Added a column for State, based on mapping the lat/longs of each named location in the file during earlier exploration.

Annual Landings from NMFS file: both Pounds and Dollars were read in as character due to commas in the number formatting; parsed these to numeric. Then calculated versions where the numbers will be smaller: Millions_of_Dollars and Millions_of_Pounds.

Seasonal head-off landings of white shrimp: added two columns for better ordering, because ‘Win_Spr_Sum’ is Jan-July, and ‘Fall’ is Aug-Dec of each year. Added Months to show this, and Period where Fall is 1 and Win_Spr_Sum is 2. Otherwise Fall appears first in the data frame due to alphabetical ordering; but chronologically it should be 2nd.

Generated data file(s): Data frames were modified as described above, and written to data/intermediate/adultCommercial_dfs.RData (the single .RData file contains multiple data frames):

landings_annual
landings_seas
tripTick_abund

Other notes about data:

landings_seas only represents two states: GA and SC. The annual landings and trip ticket data frames also include NC.

title: 13  Adults - landings and trip tickets
text:
13.1 Landings Data

Brown Shrimp
Use annual data for brown shrimp, because it corresponds to the life cycle and shrimp year. Three states are represented in this dataset. NC is not represented elsewhere, so it is removed and we will focus only on GA and SC.


Code
brn_landings <- landings_annual |> 
    janitor::clean_names() |> 
    filter(species == "brown",
           state != "NORTH CAROLINA") |> 
    select(shrimp_year = year,
           species,
           state,
           pounds)

brn_abund <- brn_landings |> 
    mutate(survey = case_when(state == "GEORGIA" ~ "GA",
                              state == "SOUTH CAROLINA" ~ "SC",
                              .default = "PROBLEM"),
           life_stage = "adult.landings",
           abundance_measure = "pounds",
           abundance = pounds,
           sqrt_abundance = sqrt(abundance)) |> 
    select(all_of(sel_order_annual)) |> 
    arrange(shrimp_year, species, survey)




Code
ggplot(brn_abund,
       aes(x = shrimp_year,
           y = abundance,
           col = survey)) +
    geom_point(size = 2)








Figure 13.1





For white shrimp landings, we only have totals across the states of GA and SC. For Juvenile and Subadult stages (both species), we averaged the values from the two states.
Here, I calculated both ways, and only later realized they would be exactly the same once normalized - because averaging is just dividing the total by 2, for all samples; so they all stay the same relative to each other when you re-scale.
Because ‘mean’ will probably be primary, the variable names that match those of other files will contain values using the mean across GA and SC. “sum” will be appended to variable names using a total across the two states, in case such values are needed later.


Code
brn_byShrimpYear <- brn_abund |> 
    group_by(species, life_stage, shrimp_year) |> 
    summarize(abundance_sum = sum(abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
              abundance = mean(abundance, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
    ungroup() |> 
    mutate(sqrt_abundance_sum = sqrt(abundance_sum),
           sqrt_abundance = sqrt(abundance),
           survey = "Landings, GA and SC",
           abundance_measure = "mean over 2 states; sum also provided") |> 
    select(all_of(sel_order_annual_extra)) |> 
    group_by(species) |> 
    mutate(abundanceIndex_fullTimePeriod = as.vector(scale(sqrt_abundance)),
           abundanceIndexSum_fullTimePeriod = as.vector(scale(sqrt_abundance_sum))) |> 
    ungroup()

brn_abund_commontime <- brn_byShrimpYear |> 
    select(species, shrimp_year, sqrt_abundance, sqrt_abundance_sum) |> 
    filter(shrimp_year %in% common_shrimpYears) |> 
    group_by(species) |> 
    mutate(abundanceIndex_commonTimePeriod = as.vector(scale(sqrt_abundance)),
           abundanceIndexSum_commonTimePeriod = as.vector(scale(sqrt_abundance_sum))) |> 
    ungroup()

brn_byShrimpYear <- left_join(brn_byShrimpYear, 
                              brn_abund_commontime)


Write out.


Code
# by state
write.csv(brn_abund,
          here::here(out_path_detailed,
                     "adult.landings.brown_byStateAndShrimpYear.csv"),
          na = "",
          row.names = FALSE)

# combined with index
write.csv(brn_byShrimpYear,
          here::here(out_path,
                     "adult.landings.brown_byShrimpYear.csv"),
          na = "",
          row.names = FALSE)




White Shrimp
Using seasonal data for white shrimp, to separate non-spawning adults (time period 2 for a calendar year, season Fall, Months Aug-Dec) from spawners (time period 1 of the next calendar year, season Winter-Spring-Summer, months Jan-July).
The input file contained heads-off landings from SC and GA.


Code
# Fall = Aug-Dec  - make shrimp_year =  year
# Win_Spr_Sum = Jan-Jul - make shrimp_year = year - 1

wht_landings <- landings_seas |> 
    mutate(shrimp_year = case_when(season == "Fall" ~ Year,
                                   .default = Year - 1),
           life_stage = case_when(season == "Fall" ~ "adult.nonspawning.landings",
                                  .default = "adult.spawning.landings"),
           survey = "landings",
           species = "white",
           abundance_measure = "head-off weight, sum of SC and GA",
           abundance = lbs_headOff,
           sqrt_abundance = sqrt(abundance)) |> 
    filter(shrimp_year >= 1979,
           shrimp_year <= 2022) |> 
    janitor::clean_names() |> 
    select(any_of(sel_order_monthly),
           season, sqrt_abundance) |> 
    relocate(season, .after = "year")


Generate abundance index. Handling a little differently because there are two life stages in here (spawning and non-spawning adults).


Code
# abundance index, full time
wht_abund <- wht_landings |> 
    group_by(species, life_stage) |> 
    mutate(abundanceIndex_fullTimePeriod = as.vector(scale(sqrt_abundance))) |> 
    ungroup()

# abundance index, common time
wht_abund_commonTime <- wht_abund |> 
    select(species, life_stage, shrimp_year, sqrt_abundance) |> 
    filter(shrimp_year %in% common_shrimpYears) |> 
    group_by(species, life_stage) |> 
    mutate(abundanceIndex_commonTimePeriod = as.vector(scale(sqrt_abundance))) |> 
    ungroup()

wht_abund <- left_join(wht_abund, 
                       wht_abund_commonTime) |> 
    rename(calendar_year = year) |> 
    select(survey, species, shrimp_year, life_stage,
           calendar_year, season,
           everything())




Code
ggplot(wht_abund,
       aes(x = shrimp_year,
           y = abundanceIndex_fullTimePeriod,
           col = life_stage)) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_line() +
    theme_bw()








Figure 13.2: Abundance Index for white shrimp, by spawning vs. non-spawning adults







Code
ggplot(wht_abund) +
    geom_histogram(aes(x = abundanceIndex_fullTimePeriod)) +
    facet_wrap(~life_stage)


Write out white shrimp data. Both ‘adult’ life stages are in the single file.


Code

          here::here(out_path,
                     "adult.landings.white_byShrimpYear.csv"),
          na = "",
          row.names = FALSE)

title: 13  Adults - landings and trip tickets
text:
13.2 Trip Ticket Data
I intended to compile to annual totals, but in early years there are big differences in reporting frequencies. So the only files I will write out will contain the ‘Wave’, which is the 2-month period of reporting. I will not compile to annual values or abundance indices.
Would probably be best to pull out a wave or two and use those as an index. Waves 3, 4, and 5 seem to be pretty consistently reported after about 2000.

Brown Shrimp


Code
brn_tt_byState <- tripTick_abund |> 
    filter(Species == "brown",
           State %in% c("GA", "SC")) |> 
    mutate(shrimp_year = Year,
           life_stage = "adult.triptickets",
           survey = paste0("Trip tickets, ", State),
           pseudodate = lubridate::ymd(paste(Year, Wave_start, 15))) |> 
    select(pseudodate, Year, Wave, shrimp_year, survey, life_stage, 
           annland, numdeal, numfisher, CPUE_approx) |> 
    arrange(Year, Wave)

# average or add the states together, within wave
brn_tt <- brn_tt_byState |> 
    summarize(.by = c(pseudodate, shrimp_year, Wave, life_stage),
              annland_sum = sum(annland, na.rm = TRUE),
              numdeal_sum = sum(numdeal, na.rm = TRUE),
              numfisher_sum = sum(numfisher, na.rm = TRUE),
              CPUE_approx = mean(CPUE_approx, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
    mutate(CPUE_approx_sumGAandSC = annland_sum/numfisher_sum,
           survey = "Trip tickets, GA and SC",
           abundance_measure = "mean CPUE across states; with CPUE based on sum provided")




Code
ggplot(brn_tt,
       aes(x = pseudodate,
           y = CPUE_approx)) +
    geom_line(col = "gray50") +
    geom_point(aes(col = Wave,
                   shape = Wave),
               size = 2) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    labs(title = "Brown Shrimp",
         x = "Date")








Figure 13.3: Approximate CPUE for GA & SC combined (mean CPUE per time period across states) for brown shrimp by time period. Notice the vastly different reporting frequencies before about 2000.







Code
# by state & wave
write.csv(brn_tt_byState,
          here::here(out_path_detailed,
                     "adult.triptickets.brown_01byStateAndWave.csv"),
          na = "",
          row.names = FALSE)

# by state & shrimp year
write.csv(brn_tt,
          here::here(out_path_detailed,
                     "adult.triptickets.brown_02byWave.csv"),
          na = "",
          row.names = FALSE)




White Shrimp
For whites, ideally I would compile to the same seasons reported in landings: Jan-Jul and Aug-Dec. However the waves here split; Jul-Aug are combined. Per advice from a work group member, July landings are negligible and this wave should be dominated by August landings, so we will count them with Fall/non-spawning shrimp.
There are most likely differences in when reporting happened seasonally, as with brown shrimp, so I will again only compile to “Wave”.


Code
wht_tt_byState <- tripTick_abund |> 
    filter(Species == "white",
           State %in% c("GA", "SC")) |> 
    mutate(shrimp_year = case_when(WAVE <= 3 ~ Year - 1,
                                   WAVE >= 4 ~ Year),
           life_stage = case_when(WAVE <= 3 ~ "adult.spawning.triptickets",
                                  WAVE >= 4 ~ "adult.nonspawning.triptickets"),
           survey = paste0("Trip tickets, ", State),
           pseudodate = lubridate::ymd(paste(Year, Wave_start, 15))) |> 
    select(Year, pseudodate, Wave, shrimp_year, survey, life_stage, 
           annland, numdeal, numfisher, CPUE_approx)

# add the states together, within wave
wht_tt <- wht_tt_byState |> 
    summarize(.by = c(pseudodate, shrimp_year, Wave, life_stage),
              annland = sum(annland, na.rm = TRUE),
              numdeal = sum(numdeal, na.rm = TRUE),
              numfisher = sum(numfisher, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
    mutate(CPUE_approx = annland/numfisher,
           survey = "Trip tickets, GA + SC total")




Code
ggplot(wht_tt,
       aes(x = pseudodate,
           y = CPUE_approx)) +
    geom_line(col = "gray50") +
    geom_point(aes(col = life_stage,
                   shape = Wave),
               size = 2) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    labs(title = "White Shrimp",
         x = "Date")








Figure 13.4: Approximate CPUE for GA & SC combined (added together) for white shrimp by time period. Notice the vastly different reporting frequencies before about 2000.





Looks like there was a lot going on before about 1995 so let’s filter that data.


Code
ggplot(filter(wht_tt, shrimp_year >= 1995),
       aes(x = pseudodate,
           y = CPUE_approx)) +
    geom_line(col = "gray50") +
    geom_point(aes(col = life_stage,
                   shape = Wave),
               size = 2) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    labs(title = "White Shrimp")








Figure 13.5: Approximate CPUE for GA & SC combined (added together) for white shrimp by time period, starting in 1995





There are several years where Wave 2 is missing (triangle), but 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6 seem pretty consistent in this time period (post-1995).
All years are included in these output files.

write.csv(wht_tt_byState,
          here::here(out_path_detailed,
                     "adult.triptickets.white_01byStateAndWave.csv"),
          na = "",
          row.names = FALSE)

# by state & shrimp year
write.csv(wht_tt,
          here::here(out_path_detailed,
                     "adult.triptickets.white_02byWave.csv"),
          na = "",
          row.names = FALSE)

totalDays <- names(brn)[str_starts(names(brn), "totalDays")]
comp_grid <- expand.grid(life_stage = levels(brn$life_stage),
                         totalDays = totalDays)
comp_grid <- comp_grid |> 
    mutate(longestSpell = str_replace(totalDays, "totalDays", "longestSpell"))

comp_out <- list()

for(i in 1:nrow(comp_grid)){
    comp.stage <- comp_grid[i, "life_stage"]
    comp.totalDays <- comp_grid[i, "totalDays"]
    comp.longestSpell <- comp_grid[i, "longestSpell"]
    
    # subset the data frame
    comp.rows <- which(brn$life_stage == comp.stage)
    comp.cols <- which(names(brn) %in% c("shrimp_year", "abundIndex", as.character(comp.totalDays), as.character(comp.longestSpell)))
    
    
    comb <- brn[comp.rows, comp.cols]
    names(comb) <- c("shrimp_year", "abund_index", "totalDays", "longestSpell")
    
    # correlation and CI for total # days
    corr_totalDays <- SpearmanRho(comb$totalDays,
                                  comb$abund_index,
                                  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
                                  conf.level = 0.95)
    corr_totalDays <- data.frame("totalDays_estimate" = corr_totalDays["rho"],
                                 "totalDays_ciLow" = corr_totalDays["lwr.ci"],
                                 "totalDays_ciHigh" = corr_totalDays["upr.ci"],
                                 row.names = NULL)
    
    # correlation and CI for longest # days
    corr_mostDays <- SpearmanRho(comb$longestSpell,
                                 comb$abund_index,
                                 use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
                                 conf.level = 0.95)
    corr_mostDays <- data.frame("consecDays_estimate" = corr_mostDays["rho"],
                                "consecDays_ciLow" = corr_mostDays["lwr.ci"],
                                "consecDays_ciHigh" = corr_mostDays["upr.ci"],
                                row.names = NULL)
    
    corr_out <- cbind(comp_grid[i, ],
                      corr_totalDays,
                      corr_mostDays)
    
    comp_out[[i]] <- corr_out
}

corrs_all <- bind_rows(comp_out) |> 
    mutate(totalDays_significant = case_when(totalDays_ciLow * totalDays_ciHigh > 0 ~ "yes",
                                            .default = "no"),
           consecDays_significant = case_when(consecDays_ciLow * consecDays_ciHigh > 0 ~ "yes",
                                            .default = "no"),
